articles.title: Canadian Smarties, honeycomb bars and 12 international candies way better than Snickers
articles.summary: Forget the familiar favorites and try these sweets from around the world – from caffeine-boosted chocolate drops to dragonfruit gummies – available before Halloween. ‘Tastes like Play-Doh’: the best (and worst) chocolate bars.
body: Welcome to Filter finds, a series where Guardian staff and Filter contributors share the things we love most – and think you might, too.

Every October, we set out to rot our teeth on the same high fructose corn-syrupped candies. Twizzlers! Snickers! Almond Joy! But these words have no meaning outside of the US. Beyond the hegemony of Hershey, Mars and Mondelēz lies a world of honeycomb bars, caffeine-boosted chocolate drops and dragonfruit gummies that the American mind simply can’t comprehend … though maybe our stomachs can.

We asked our Guardian colleagues for their favorite candy from around the world – be they childhood treats or souvenirs picked up through travels abroad – that we don’t need a plane ticket to try ourselves. They’re all available online, and yes, we checked: as of publication, they will all arrive before Halloween.

articles.title: Curiosity, atonement or a score to settle? Why – and how – people get through their high school reunions
articles.summary: Reunions can be riotous, scandalous or just plain awkward. Experts and attendees share how to go in prepared. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. Mike walked into his 20th high school reunion with a mission.
body: Some may relish the chance to reconnect with former friends, a former life and even a former self, but for many they are a potential hellscape, where adolescent humiliations are revived in front of a group of rapidly ageing peers.

Mike, who attended an all-boys’ school in Melbourne’s comfortable eastern suburbs, belonged to the latter group. Though he wasn’t there for vengeance. He was there to apologise. For years, he’d felt regret about the homophobic bullying a friend had faced at school. Although Mike never targeted the boy himself, he “always felt guilty about not doing enough”.
He knew he couldn’t change the past, but he hoped to clear his conscience and apologise for not intervening.

The pair did connect, and atonements were made. Mike, though, left with new laments. “It was a fumbly conversation that ended up with him consoling me about not having to feel guilty. I felt like a bit of a dick, accidentally getting an old friend who’d experienced genuinely horrific bullying to walk me through my feelings.”
points: Reunions can be riotous, scandalous or just plain awkward.

articles.title: Fridge or not? What’s the best way to store bread?
articles.summary: Our experts have some airtight advice on stopping your loaf from going stale – and even freshening it up again – but whatever you do, keep it out of the fridge. What’s the best way to store bread? Beeswax wraps, plastic bags, fridge – I’ve tried everything except a bread bin.
body: To combat this, Handschuh stores her loaf at room temperature in a greaseproof paper bag (ie, the one you bring it home in): “That’s probably the best way – no plastic. And, yes, you can use beeswax wrap, but that’s expensive and you shouldn’t have to go and buy some just for storing bread.”

A paper bag is also Rachel Morgan’s preference: “I’d avoid a bread bin, though,” says the co-founder of Twelve Triangles in Edinburgh. “That can trap moisture, so the bread gets a bit sweaty, which softens the crust and encourages mould.”

Reheating is your gateway to regaining freshness: “Warming bread enables the water to evaporate and for the starch to reactivate,” Handschuh says. So, if your bread is a couple of days’ old, “stick it in the oven for five to 10 minutes, and it should stay fresh for a day or two longer”.

articles.title: ‘How green are our valleys?’: in the footsteps of miners on south Wales’s new forest trail
articles.summary: The first stage of an ambitious new hiking route that will link woodlands across Wales takes walkers into the wild hills above the valleys’ old mining villages. Bracken and heather ripple across the plateau.
body: I’m hiking the new Llwybr Coedwig Cymru Trail, or Wales Forest Trail. Running from Porthkerry Park, near Barry, to Pont Walby, close to Glynneath, this 50-mile (80km) pilot route is the first section of what the National Forest for Wales hopes will eventually be a trail linking woodlands across the length and breadth of Wales: a sylvan counterpart to the Wales Coast Path.

My father grew up in one of the valleys’ mining villages and, when I visited relatives there as a child, the disconnection of those post-industrial communities from the wild hills that loomed above them was striking. Mountain bikers have long discovered the region’s potential, but walkers still tend to head for the more obvious trails that wind through the national parks or along the coast. This pilot trail seems a good excuse to explore untapped footpaths.

With the sea behind me, I set off from the oak leaf sculpture that marks the trail’s start. The viaduct ahead once carried coal to Barry docks, but today it stands over Caffe Matteo, busy with dog walkers sipping cappuccinos. Leaving them behind, I cross the park between the soft greens of birch and oak trees.

articles.title: Is it Safe to Travel to Paris Right Now Amidst the France Protests?
articles.summary: As France protests and unrest continue unfolding across the capital, we share practical advice on where to stay, what to avoid, and how to navigate the city safely.
body: If there is one thing that the French know how to do, it is fight for their rights. It’s not for the goodness of politicians' hearts that university fees in France are still $200 for a bachelor's degree but thanks to a population that refuses to back down when their rights are being threatened.

Since September, French high school students have been protesting for better conditions, especially in suburban areas often forgotten by institutions. The movement has reached almost unprecedented proportions, with other sectors joining the students, demanding better learning conditions and fighting against the cost-of-living crisis, hike in fuel prices, and erosion of social welfare.

articles.title: I Need a Hero: How Statement Items Ruled the Spring 2027 Collections
articles.summary: On the runways, designers are making their mark with eccentric accessories, but shopping it is more than just a maximalist revival. “It’s almost like buying a piece of history,” said Jalil Johnson.
body: What do Prada’s 63 skirts, Chanel’s 83 pairs of shoes, and Celine’s bug-eyed sunglasses and oversized belts have in common? They’re all hero items fresh from the spring 2027 runways. These are not the Gucci double G belts or Balenciaga logo T-shirts of a pre-pandemic logomania scene, nor are they purely part of a Man Repeller-era eccentric revival. These hero items’ particular funk is part of a new system of signaling in a more fashion-savvy digital age, one where a pair of pump’s contrasting teal toe cap says it all.

Much has been said about the end of quiet luxury—the vibrant menswear collections over the summer finally squashed that conversation entirely, actually. Meanwhile, in the background, favorable sentiments about statement pieces have been stewing. A good argument could be made that the hero item’s return really kicked off with Dario Vitale’s lone, glorious collection for Versace where rumpled, sensual savants ran supreme. “Bold, graphic and colorful, [Vitale’s] pencil skirts and shoes were on every industry insider in September,” Chloe King, of Neiman Marcus and Saks Fifth Avenue, told Vogue.

The outlet praises its gorgeous picture quality, excellent contrast, and well-balanced colors. It has perfect black levels with no light bloom and uses LG’s webOS smart TV platform, like most current LG TVs. It’s also strengthened by features like AI dialogue enhancement, which helps improve the internal 2.2-channel audio system.

It has a native 120Hz refresh rate, with VRR up to 165Hz, and supports AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync, making it a solid choice for gamers. Ultimately, if vibrant, bright, and accurate 4K OLED picture quality is your priority but you don’t want to spend the $3,000 that some competitors with similar features cost, you won’t find much better than the 55-inch LG OLED Evo C6 at this price point—as long as you’re OK with the lack of Wi-Fi 6.

articles.title: Adrian Danchig-Waring Bid Farewell to New York City Ballet With a Post-Show Rave
articles.summary: To sign off, Danchig-Waring didn’t just curate a matinee program. Rather, fitting for an artist with an expansive sense of the medium’s possibilities, he also gathered his friends for a post-show tropical rave at Performance Space in the East Village.
body: How do you measure a storied ballet career? You can look at time spent in the ranks, shaped by rigorous training and its corresponding toll on the body. Or repertoire: the historic roles a dancer has come to define in their own way, along with the new commissions they’ve breathed into being. You can consider the reverberation of influence, both on younger dancers and the company itself. And then there’s an energetic quality, at times radiating light and other times shining it—with or without pulsing strobes—on others.

All of these facets were front of mind on Sunday when the New York City Ballet principal Adrian Danchig-Waring took his final bow with the company, beside a heap of ribbon-tied white roses. Ever since the California native moved into the dorms at the School of American Ballet, its sister institution, in 2001, and joined NYCB two years later, he has been a quietly majestic interpreter of George Balanchine’s canon. Along the way, Danchig-Waring has been equally engaged with today’s dancemakers, both in the studio and in his role as the artistic director of the New York Choreographic Institute.

articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders—and Ricky Martin and Pedro Sampaio—Left Brazil Thunderstruck at the NFL’s Rio Debut
articles.summary: Behind the scenes with America’s Sweethearts as they met the loudest crowd of their lives, fused “Thunderstruck” with Brazilian funk, and turned Maracanã into a dance floor.
body: “I can’t believe cheerleaders are actually real, ” exclaimed a fan who had come to Maracanã Stadium specifically to see the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders. Minutes earlier, the squad delivered the high kicks and synchronized jump splits of its signature “Thunderstruck” routine, ushering in the NFL’s first-ever game in Rio de Janeiro.

The NFL is staging a record nine international games this season, each with the trappings of a mini Super Bowl Some 5,200 miles from their base, the Dallas Cowboys were the designated home team against the Baltimore Ravens, and they brought the traditions, smoke machines, and rhinestones of a typical AT&T Stadium outing with them.

The Cowboys built their brand as “America’s Team”—and they couldn’t do it without their cheerleaders. Netflix’s America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, filming its fourth season while in Brazil, has taken viewers inside the lives and grueling training regimes of these 36 women.
